questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Let ${σ}_{1}, {σ}_{2}, {σ}_{3}$ be planes passing through the origin. Assume that ${σ}_{1}$ is perpendicular to the vector $\left(1, 1, 1\right)$,~${σ}_{2}$ is perpendicular to a vector $\left(a, b, c\right) and {σ}_{3}$ is perpendicular to the vector $\left(a^{2}, b^{2}, c^{2}\right)$. What are all the positive values of $a, b and c$ so that ${σ}_{1} ∩ {σ}_{2} ∩ {σ}_{3}$ is a single point?
options: Any positive value of $a, b$, and $c$ other than $1$

Any positive values of $a, b$ and $c$ where either $a e b, b e c$
or $a e c$
Any three distinct positive values of $a, b$ and $c$
There exist no such positive real numbers $a, b$, and $c$
questions.solution:
According to given information equation of planes&

${σ}_{1}; x + y + z = {d}_{1}$

${σ}_{2}: ax + by + cz = {d}_{2}$

and ${σ}_{3}: a^{2}x + b^{2}y + c^{2}z = {d}_{3}$

Now, for unique solution $\Delta \ne 0$.

and $\Delta = \left|\begin{cases}1 & 1 & 1 \\ a & b & c \\ a^{2} & b^{2} & c^{2}\end{cases}\right|$

On applying ${c}_{2} \to {c}_{2} - {c}_{1}$ and ${c}_{3} \to {c}_{3} - {c}_{1}$

$\Delta = \left|\begin{cases}1 & 0 & 0 \\ a & b - a & c - a \\ a^{2} & b^{2} - a^{2} & c^{2} - a^{2}\end{cases}\right| = \left(b - a\right)\left(c - a\right)$

$\left|\begin{cases}1 & 0 & 0 \\ a & 1 & 1 \\ a^{2} & b + a & c + a\end{cases}\right|$

On applying ${c}_{3} \to {c}_{3} - {c}_{2}$

$\left(b - a\right)\left(c - a\right)\left|\begin{cases}1 & 0 & 0 \\ a & 1 & 0 \\ a^{2} & b + a & c - b\end{cases}\right|$

$= \left(a - b\right) \left(b - c\right)\left(c - a\right)$

So, if $a, b$ and $c$ has any three distinct values then \Delta \ne0$.

$
